npcs.name: Warden Telyne Aryon
npcs.greet: Warden of the Hlaalu canton's stairs, sera. Four hundred and twelve of them, and I know which ones are loose.

npcs.name: Tosa the Cantonkeeper
npcs.greet: Water goes where water wants. My work is to disagree with it politely, with gates.

npcs.name: Brother Fendil
npcs.greet: A pilgrim! Wonderful. The Last Stair is the best stair. It costs a little extra, for the view.

npcs.name: Ruvene Olvyn
npcs.greet: The Sunken Lantern. Rooms by the night, soup by the bowl, and the stairs to your room by the flight. Don't look at me like that; I counted them.

npcs.name: Bethal Aryon
npcs.greet: Bethal's Dry Goods and Wet Alibis. Umbrellas, oilskins, and a good word for a bad evening. Yes, it never rains. That is why they are cheap.

npcs.name: Hlenil Dro
npcs.greet: Ferry to any canton, any hour, and I'll only tell you the shortcuts if you stop asking what's underneath.

npcs.name: Ilnoth the Pit-Caller
npcs.greet: Ladies, gentlemen, and those who prefer not to say! Tonight's fight is real. The odds are not. Come, place a coin.

npcs.name: Archcanon Teris Ulvani
npcs.greet: The Temple is patient. It has had to be. Do sit. Nobody is listening, which is rare in Mournhold, so let us use it.

npcs.name: Mistress Hlaren
npcs.greet: Forty stalls, one rule: nothing sold here is stolen. Everything sold here was stolen *once*. It is the first sale that matters.

npcs.name: Old Sedyn
npcs.greet: Down there, the same streets, and the same lamps. Only the ghosts pay rent. I take a lantern and a bad knee and I go down every Sundas.

npcs.name: Gaela Nelvan
npcs.greet: The Silver Samovar, sera: tea, honey-cake, and a back table where deals take place. Do not ask which deals. I serve the tea cold when I'm listening.

npcs.name: Orlen Veloth
npcs.greet: Hlaalu bronze, Redoran steel, and the odd piece of Dwemer scrap that hums at night. The smithy opens when I stop shouting at the anvil.

npcs.name: Lisara Tervyn
npcs.greet: A palace archivist. Do not stack the maps and do not mention the second basement. We have all agreed that there is no second basement.

npcs.name: Ravos Dren
npcs.greet: A walk through the plaza, a lost glove found, a purse that was never there. Quite innocent. I am a student of public architecture.

npcs.name: Factor Dron Hlaalu
npcs.greet: A good merchant owns the river, not the boat. A better one owns the man who owns the boat.

npcs.name: Nilena Vandas
npcs.greet: Fence? Never. I am a freight consultant. If something was stolen before it reached me, that is a matter between it and its conscience.

npcs.name: Port-Master Orrel
npcs.greet: Silt striders do not like flat ground, loud noises, or being thanked. Be none of those, and we are friends.

npcs.name: Sirela Marvos
npcs.greet: Eight Plates. Eight plates of stew a night, no more, no fewer, and the ninth person goes hungry. It is a policy, not a shortage.

npcs.name: Dathan Selvil
npcs.greet: Cornerclub rules: no singing before sundown, no cheating after. Everything between is a negotiation.

npcs.name: Hesta Girith
npcs.greet: I make poultices and, on quieter days, apologies. Last week a customer paid me in both.

npcs.name: Rilvo Aleth
npcs.greet: Bridge duty. Keep to the left, keep moving, and do not stop to peer at the water. People have fallen off the right side, in my shift, for their trouble.

npcs.name: Councilor Brara Redoran
npcs.greet: Honour is a debt that compounds, sera. I intend to be rich in it, and I would like a witness to the count.

npcs.name: Brarmin the Egg-Miner
npcs.greet: The tunnels under this town run deeper than the town does. Mind your head, mind the eggs, and never whistle.

npcs.name: Rolfa Skar-Guard
npcs.greet: Captain. I do not bend rules, I explain them slowly. Do not make me explain them slowly.

npcs.name: Nerva Hlavis
npcs.greet: The Rat in the Pot, sera, and no, there is no rat. There was a rat. There is a pot. You will find the connection is purely nominal.

npcs.name: Velan Arethi
npcs.greet: Chitin armour, bonemold, and a good word for your elbows. If it breaks, you may bring it back. If you broke it, you may not.

npcs.name: Tevra Dren
npcs.greet: Marshmerrow, hackle-lo, trama root and a very patient face. Poisons? Not here, no. Never here. Ask Rilu behind the shell.

npcs.name: Durgul Ash-Born
npcs.greet: I am a duellist for hire. Not an assassin. The difference is a witness and a very small piece of paper.

npcs.name: Magister Gaenor Dreth
npcs.greet: Do not curtsey. I am levitating, you see, and the angle is unflattering for both of us. Something to wager? I am so very bored.

npcs.name: Magister Ulveni Rathra
npcs.greet: My tower has fourteen floors, eleven guardians and one very short temper. Which of the three were you hoping to meet?

npcs.name: Skeema the Sporekeeper
npcs.greet: Careful. The blue ones sing. The green ones listen. I have not decided what the grey ones do, and I would like not to find out in company.

npcs.name: Apprentice Veya
npcs.greet: Seven years I have carried my master's slippers up and down fourteen floors. I want to learn something that is not a cobweb.

npcs.name: Dalyne Hlaren
npcs.greet: The Gateway Inn, sera. Every room has a window. Not every window has a view of the same place twice. Do not ask; the Magisters like it.

npcs.name: Sergeant Maro Gallus
npcs.greet: Wolverine Hall. Imperial garrison. We keep the peace, we keep the books and we keep very, very far from the Telvanni towers.

npcs.name: Fennik Sul
npcs.greet: Spore & Sundry. Dried caps, glass jars, fumigation salts. If a jar glows when you open it, please close it again and say nothing.

npcs.name: Keeper Salvu
npcs.greet: The dead are not quiet. They are polite. There is a difference, and it is the difference between a household and a haunting.

npcs.name: Elder Nerevi
npcs.greet: Outlanders do not walk the Row. Not out of cruelty, sera. Out of arithmetic: the Row has twelve houses and each house has a guest list.

npcs.name: Aldrin the Restless
npcs.greet: I have dug four hundred graves in this town. I will not dig the fifth one they asked for. Do not ask which. Do not ask why.

npcs.name: Mirele Sathil
npcs.greet: The Pilgrims' Rest. Candlelit alcoves, quiet suppers, and no sermons after dark. We count the candles. Do not be offended; the dead count them too.

npcs.name: Tadrik Ulvo
npcs.greet: Funerary wares: shrouds, ash-urns, memorial lanterns and an excellent line in sympathy cards. We do not do refunds. The dead never complain.

npcs.name: Warden Ilu Dren
npcs.greet: I keep the canton lift. Three bells down, three bells up, no exceptions for weather, kings or prayer.

npcs.name: Dren the Lavacutter
npcs.greet: Twenty years I have cut glass out of the lava channels. Never once have I looked at it straight. A man who does gets a certain look.

npcs.name: Sister Mavia
npcs.greet: I collect ashes, sera. Not the dead's. The living's. Everyone leaves a little behind. I am only the one who sweeps it.

npcs.name: Orvyn Hlaalo
npcs.greet: The Cinder Cup. Warm rooms, warm soup, warmer company. It is also the only inn in Morrowind where you pay for the cooling.

npcs.name: Kesha-Teb
npcs.greet: Glass, obsidian, ash-salts, a small selection of lava-polished jewellery that is, I promise, not cursed. Not recently.

npcs.name: Legate Corvus Pello
npcs.greet: Order is a habit, not a gift. I intend to keep the habit. A name will be handed to me by evening, and I will arrest the man it belongs to.

npcs.name: Aryn the Informer
npcs.greet: Information is a river, sera: it flows downhill, to whoever stands lowest. I stand very low indeed. Coin, please.

npcs.name: Chaplain Loris
npcs.greet: The garrison's confessions are the shortest in the Empire. Nobody does anything wrong. Nobody does anything at all. It is a very quiet war.

npcs.name: Marga Ironhand
npcs.greet: The Bastion's Heel. Two kinds of beer: the one the garrison drinks and the one it pretends it doesn't. I'll serve you the second.

npcs.name: Guardsman Tolan Veyl
npcs.greet: South gate, third bell. Quiet shift. Always a quiet shift. Do not ask about the purse; it is for my mother.

npcs.name: Felmin Rothal
npcs.greet: The Company buys, ships and sells. Dunmer silk, Imperial steel, anything with a margin. Do ask about the margin. It is the one thing we do not hide.

relics.name: Tosa's Sounding Line
relics.desc: A weighted cord knotted every fathom, with a stripe of fresh stone-dust at fourteen.

relics.name: Bronze Gate-Wheel
relics.desc: The hand-wheel of a canton sluice, cut off its shaft with a mason's saw.

relics.name: Fenril's Dry-Tithe Ledger
relics.desc: Water sold by the cistern to a plantation, under a clerk's neat hand and the Warden's own seal.

relics.name: Crate of Oilskin Umbrellas
relics.desc: Forty oilskin umbrellas, waxed and furled. The handles rattle faintly.

relics.name: Bazaar Contract Map
relics.desc: A courier contract for forty crates, with a street plan inked in the margin where the crates are not meant to go.

relics.name: Mirror-Plaza Key
relics.desc: A black iron key shaped like a plaza fountain, cold to the touch, warm when you stand in old Mournhold.

relics.name: Seal of the Sunken Vault
relics.desc: A wax seal pressed into a lump of Dwemer brass; the pattern is the Palace plan, reversed.

relics.name: Dron's South-Bank Ledger
relics.desc: A merchant prince's river ledger, warm from a fence's hands.

relics.name: Manor Council Ledger
relics.desc: The second ledger: a Council steward's private tallies, half in code.

relics.name: The Bridge Ledger
relics.desc: The third book: a bridge toll-keeper's list of whom the river owes.

relics.name: Grey Girl's Letter
relics.desc: A plain letter, sealed in plain wax, addressed to nobody at all.

relics.name: The Poisoned Blade
relics.desc: A Redoran duelling blade, its edge slick with a bitter green resin. It was not made to cut flesh. It was made to be borrowed.

relics.name: Proof of the Egg-Mine Poisoner
relics.desc: A clay jar of resin and a Hlaalu apothecary's receipt, tied with a Redoran ribbon.

relics.name: Ulveni's Singing Teapot
relics.desc: A squat enamelled teapot. It hums three notes when lifted, and sulks when set down.

relics.name: Gaenor's Wager Slip
relics.desc: A slip of cream paper: "One tower. One item. Three days. Loser pays in an honest Telvanni currency: embarrassment."

relics.name: Sathil Heirloom Ring
relics.desc: A plain bone-white ring engraved on the inside with a name that has been filed away.

relics.name: The Unfinished Deed
relics.desc: A farm deed with one signature and an unsigned space, stained with candle-wax.

relics.name: The Last Ash
relics.desc: A funerary urn of grey ash, still faintly warm, still holding the shape of a hand.

relics.name: The Failed Heat-Vent Core
relics.desc: A blackened baffle from a heat-vent, cracked straight through; the crack is a clean line that cooling alone cannot make.

relics.name: Mavia's Ash-Lantern
relics.desc: Sister Mavia's lantern, full of ashes from every living person who ever left a footprint in her cellar.

relics.name: Counterfeit Gate Key
relics.desc: A brass key with a Legion hallmark that is slightly off. It opens the south-quarter gate, and no one has noticed.

relics.name: The Gate-Seller's List
relics.desc: A list of names and sums, in a quarter-folk hand, of who bought a key and at what hour the gate opened.

quests.title: Water Under the Cantons
quests.offer: You look like someone who can keep a secret and row a boat.
quests.pitch: Three of my stairs are wet that should be dry. Stairs do not leak; the walls under them do, and the Cantonkeeper will not tell me why her ledger is lighter than the canal. Speak to her, then go and look. By boat, naturally. Everything in Vivec is by boat if you are honest about it.
quests.desc: Warden Telyne of the Hlaalu canton has wet stairs and a short water ledger. Tosa the Cantonkeeper knows more than she says.

objectives.text: Ask Tosa the Cantonkeeper about the ledger
objectives.topic: Warden Telyne says your gate-ledger is lighter than the canal.
objectives.reply: Lighter by most of a cistern a week. Someone is draining the canton below the waterline, where no ledger can see. Row out past the Hlaalu pilings at slack tide and drop this line. Fourteen fathoms. You will feel the cut.

objectives.text: Row out past the Hlaalu pilings and sound the old foundations
objectives.journal: The line ran out at fourteen fathoms and came back with a fresh chisel-mark on the stone. The cut is square. Nothing in the sea cuts squares.

objectives.text: Follow the cut into the flooded maintenance shafts
Take the gate-wheel they cut from the sluice
Face the man selling the canton its own water
Bring the wheel and the ledger to Warden Telyne
objectives.topic: The leak is sealed. The ledger has your nephew's hand and your seal.
objectives.reply: My nephew. My own sister's boy. ...Sit. Say what you will do with this, because I find I cannot decide, and I have decided everything for forty years.

choices.label: Seal the shaft and burn the ledger. The canton never hears of it.
choices.reply: Then we have both done something we will remember at the bottom of a stair. Take this. It is not payment. It is silence with a price tag.

choices.label: The Temple should count this water. Take it to them.
choices.reply: Yes. Yes, that is the right answer, and I resent you for it. Go on. I will stand beside you, in front of everyone, which is the worst place to stand.

quests.outro: The stairs were dry by the next tide. What it cost depends on whom you ask.

quests.title: A Dry Season of Silence
quests.desc: The Hlaalu canton owes you for its silence. A few debts want collecting before the water is forgotten.

objectives.text: Hear Tosa out
objectives.topic: The leak is closed. What do you want me to know?
objectives.reply: I want you to know the plantation still thirsts and will find another clerk. Hold the gate with me one night, sera, and I will pay you from the tithes nobody will ever count.

objectives.text: Hold the water-gate against the plantation's bravos

quests.outro: The gate held. Tosa pours you a measure of canal water and a better measure of sujamma.

quests.title: The Temple Counts the Water
quests.desc: The Temple is auditing the Hlaalu canton. Not everyone in it is thrilled.

objectives.text: Fetch Brother Fendil to witness the audit
objectives.topic: The Temple needs a witness who can count stairs.
objectives.reply: Counting is the one sin I have never been accused of. Lead on, and if anyone offers a bribe, please let me watch how it is done.

objectives.text: Turn back the canton factors who came to burn the books

quests.outro: The books survived, and so did Warden Telyne's good name, in the oddest way: she was the one who brought them.

quests.title: The Last Stair Is Extra
quests.offer: You have a pilgrim's boots and a sceptic's eyes.
quests.pitch: Half my guests come back from the Palace gate looking cheated. Brother Fendil sells them a blessing for the last stair, and the stair is a wall. I do not mind a swindle. I mind the swindle sending them to my bar, crying. Find out where the coin goes.
quests.desc: Ruvene Olvyn of the Sunken Lantern wants to know where Brother Fendil's 'Last Stair' coin ends up.

objectives.text: Shadow Brother Fendil as he leaves the Temple stairs at dusk
objectives.journal: Fendil doesn't go home. He crosses three bridges and a ferry, and the purse he carries is heavier than a priest's has any right to be.

objectives.text: Follow him to a canton alcove behind the canal market
objectives.journal: A hospice, small, in a stair-end nobody uses. Sixteen cots. Orphans of pilgrims who died climbing, fed on blessings that cost a stranger four drakes.

objectives.text: Confront Brother Fendil
objectives.topic: I followed you. The coin buys cots, not wine.
objectives.reply: Then you know the worst of me. The Temple's stipend would feed four. The pilgrims' pity feeds sixteen. Tell Warden Telyne and the hospice closes. Tell no one and I go on lying to the lonely. Choose, and forgive me.

choices.label: Report him. The Temple should fund the hospice honestly.
choices.reply: Honestly. Imagine it. I will be fined and the cots will be counted and perhaps, perhaps, someone will notice them.

choices.label: Say nothing. And leave a purse on the third cot.
choices.reply: Bless you, in a way that costs nothing. Pilgrims will still hit the wall. They will not know that the wall is a roof.

quests.outro: Ruvene refunded three pilgrims out of her own till and refused to explain why.

quests.title: The Reigning Champion Falls Down
quests.offer: Do you gamble, stranger, or only fight?
quests.pitch: Kemel-Ze has won thirty-one bouts and I would swear on the Tribunal that he lost four of them. A champion who falls down on cue pays whoever knows the cue. I want to know who. Win a bout of your own and let me watch what happens at the bookmaker's window.
quests.desc: Ilnoth the Pit-Caller suspects the Arena canton's champion throws fights on someone's cue.

objectives.text: Win a bout against the reigning champion
Tell Ilnoth the champion yielded to you
objectives.topic: He yielded the moment I swung wide. Not to me. To the window.
objectives.reply: Wide, yes, I saw. He glanced at the bookmaker's boy. The boy glanced at the second balcony. Someone up there wears the Hlaalu green and has never once bet the same side as the crowd. Ask the boy. Gently. He bites.

objectives.text: Slip into the bookmaker's cellar under the pit
objectives.journal: Slates stacked to the ceiling: each bout, each purse, and beside each in neat chalk the word 'Dron' with a number. A single patron has been quietly buying fights for two years.

objectives.text: Decide what Ilnoth does with the slates
objectives.topic: The patron is a Hlaalu factor. Two years of throws. Your move.
objectives.reply: I can name him from the stage, which ruins a man in Vivec. Or I can sell him the slates, and eat well, and the fights stay crooked but the crowd stays loud. I am a showman. Say the word.

choices.label: Name him from the stage.
choices.reply: Then the crowd gets the best bout of the year, and none of us fight in it.

choices.label: Sell him the slates. Split it with me.
choices.reply: The odds were never honest. At least now I am paid for it.

quests.outro: The pit still roars. Whether it roars at the truth depends on which of you won the cellar.

quests.title: Umbrellas for the Dry
quests.offer: You want an umbrella. Everyone wants an umbrella, eventually.
quests.pitch: My stock is a shipwreck's worth of oilskin umbrellas that never reached me. The wreck is out past the Ebonheart road: Lost Shipwreck, they call it, cheerfully. Bring back the crates. I'll not ask you what else is in them, and you will not ask me why I do not ask.
quests.desc: Bethal Aryon wants her umbrella crates recovered from the Lost Shipwreck. She is oddly incurious about what else is in them.

objectives.text: Find the wreck where her umbrellas went down
Drive off the scavengers and the drowned crew
Take the umbrella crate from the hold
Bring the crate to Bethal
objectives.topic: Forty umbrellas, and one more thing: the handles are hollow and packed with moon sugar.
objectives.reply: Hollow handles. How curious. How dry my shop would be, without them. A lady in my position cannot be seen to sell sugar; a lady in my position can be seen to sell umbrellas. The Fane's Customs men are not curious. Are you?

choices.label: Keep selling. I want a cut, and the handles sealed tighter.
choices.reply: A partner! Splendid. Mind the rain; it does not fall here, and neither do the Customs.

choices.label: I'm turning the crate over to the Customs.
choices.reply: Then I wish you a damp and honest life. You will not be buying here again, sera.

quests.outro: Vivec has never been so well-covered against weather that does not exist.

quests.title: Beneath the Twin City
quests.offer: You look like someone who reads the fine print.
quests.pitch: A courier contract came through my stall for forty crates of lamp-oil. The route, drawn in the margin, runs not through the bazaar but under it. Somebody wants a way into Old Mournhold, and wants a bazaar guildmaster's stamp to look innocent. I would like to know who, before I am blamed.
quests.desc: Mistress Hlaren has a courier contract whose margin hides a map beneath the Great Bazaar.

objectives.text: Take the contract and ask what the margin means
objectives.topic: Show me the margin map.
objectives.reply: The crates are never meant to arrive, sera. The route ends at a drain under the Godsreach terrace. Find the sexton called Sedyn; he leads a lantern down there every Sundas and he is the only soul I trust with a drain.

objectives.text: Find Old Sedyn and ask for a way down
objectives.topic: Hlaren says you know the drain beneath the Godsreach terrace.
objectives.reply: Know it? I have a favourite spot in it. Go by the third lamp and say nothing to the ghosts; they take it personally. The twin plaza lies at the bottom. Whoever drew that map wants the vault under the twin Palace. Mind the Mirror-Warden. It does not like visitors who walk like they own the place.

objectives.text: Enter Old Mournhold by the Godsreach drain
objectives.journal: The streets down here match the streets above, one for one, only dark and sunk and wrong-handed. A fountain runs backwards.

objectives.text: Cross the twin plaza past the ruins' ghosts
Take the mirror key from the twin fountain
Open the vault and answer the Mirror-Warden
Take the key to Archcanon Ulvani
objectives.topic: The vault is open. It is yours to seal or rob, and I am told you asked for a quiet inquiry.
objectives.reply: Quiet is the word. There is a lamp-lit reliquary below that the Temple has never admitted exists, and somebody in the Hlaalu Council has been trying to lease it. I can re-seal it, in which case it is as if you were never there. Or I can look away while it is emptied. I will not ask which I prefer. I would not like the answer.

choices.label: Re-seal the vault. Let the twin city sleep.
choices.reply: Then it sleeps. The Temple will not forget this, and the Temple remembers everything, eventually.

choices.label: Rob it. The Temple does not need what it hides.
choices.reply: How very Mournhold of you. The back stair is open. Do not use the front.

quests.outro: The twin city lies below, patient, with its lamps lit for no one.

quests.title: The Quiet Bell
quests.desc: The Temple is grateful and wants a favour done in the quiet hours.

objectives.text: Meet the Archcanon at the dawn bell
objectives.topic: You wanted me.
objectives.reply: The one who tried to lease the vault will try again, with muscle. Stand in the courtyard at dusk. You need not do anything but be seen to wait.

objectives.text: Meet the lessor's hirelings at dusk

quests.outro: The courtyard bells rang at dusk and nobody ever mentioned why.

quests.title: Hot Brass
quests.desc: What you took from the vault is warm to the touch, and someone is following the heat.

objectives.text: Fence the brass through Ravos Dren
objectives.topic: I have something warm. You know a buyer.
objectives.reply: I know three, and two will kill you. I will take the third. Keep walking the plaza; do not look behind you, sera, because everyone else will.

objectives.text: Shake off the Temple's watchers in the plaza

quests.outro: You ended the night richer and a little lighter in the head. The brass is somebody else's problem now.

quests.title: The Palace Has a Reflection
quests.offer: Can you hold your tongue about basements?
quests.pitch: Every palace map I catalogue is accurate except one, and it is accurate in reverse. It describes a palace that does not exist above ground. It describes the one below. Take this tracing to Old Sedyn and ask whether the maps are true; I am forbidden to ask, and cannot stop wondering.
quests.desc: Lisara Tervyn, a palace archivist, has a map of a palace that exists only under Mournhold.

objectives.text: Ask Old Sedyn if the reversed palace map is true
objectives.topic: This map shows the Palace upside down. Is it right?
objectives.reply: Right? It is the only one that is. Walk it backwards and you will find the throne room first. Do not sit in the chair. The chair is for someone, and he has been late for a long time.

objectives.text: Walk the palace plan in reverse
objectives.journal: Stairs that rise when you go down. A window with an interior sky. A door where the map said, and a note in a clerk's hand: "Do not stay."

objectives.text: Retrieve the seal from the reversed throne room
Return the seal to Lisara
objectives.topic: The reversed palace is real. I brought its seal.
objectives.reply: Then the archive has a second basement after all, and I shall have to resign or go mad. Thank you. Please never come into my office again.

quests.outro: The archivist now files the second basement under "Weather".

quests.title: Cold Tea, Warm Hands
quests.offer: Do you take your tea hot or your secrets cold?
quests.pitch: Three men sat at my back table and left one pot of tea each, undrunk and still warm, and a ledger of names behind. The ledger is not mine and the names are not kind. I would like the right people to have it. Everyone in this bazaar wants it to be the wrong people.
quests.desc: Gaela Nelvan of the Silver Samovar found a ledger of names under her back table. It belongs to someone dangerous.

objectives.text: Ask Ravos Dren who the three men were
objectives.topic: Three men, three pots of undrunk tea, a ledger.
objectives.reply: Camonna Tong collectors, sera, the bad-tempered kind. The ledger is what they lend against. Names and sums. Burn it and half of Mournhold sleeps; hand it to the Palace and the other half is arrested.

objectives.text: Meet a Legion officer behind the spice stalls
Decide who should hold the ledger
objectives.topic: Gaela has a ledger of Tong debtors. Who should hold it?
objectives.reply: The Palace will use it as a whip. The Temple would use it as a prayer-book. Neither is wholly honest. You are the only person with it who has nothing to gain. Choose a keeper. And choose quickly; the pot goes cold.

choices.label: Burn the ledger. The debts die with it.
choices.reply: Half a city sleeps tonight. The other half will ask who did this. Not you, I hope.

choices.label: Give it to the Palace. Let the law have it.
choices.reply: The cells will be full by Fredas. I do not envy the clerks who must read it aloud.

quests.outro: Gaela served the next pot hot, for the first time in a month.

quests.title: Three Ledgers, One River
quests.offer: A man in my position cannot be seen to ask what I am about to ask.
quests.pitch: Three ledgers, three banks, one rival merchant who has hidden the truth of his river dues in each. I will not be seen to take them. You, on the other hand, are nobody, which is the most useful thing in Balmora. The first is with a fence on the south bank. Pay the fence. Do not ask for a receipt.
quests.desc: Factor Dron Hlaalu wants three ledgers from three places: a fence on the south bank, the Council Manor, and a toll-keeper on the bridge.

objectives.text: Buy the first ledger from Nilena Vandas
objectives.topic: Factor Dron says you are holding something for him.
objectives.reply: A freight consultant never holds, sera; she merely receives. The ledger is in the second crate, left of the sacks. And, for free: whoever wrote it kept a second book in the Council Manor, and I am not the only one who knows.

objectives.text: Slip into the Council Manor and find the steward's ledger
objectives.journal: The Manor smells of beeswax and old favours. A ledger sits unwatched in the steward's study, which means somebody wants it taken.

objectives.text: Take the second ledger from the steward's study
Meet the toll-keeper's ambush on the high bridge
Hand the three ledgers to Dron
objectives.topic: All three. River dues, Manor tallies, and the bridge toll. What now?
objectives.reply: Now I own the river a little more than yesterday, and you are the only person who knows the number of ledgers I needed. I could pay you. I could sell all three to the Temple, who would pay far better and ruin my rival. Or burn them, and be clean. It is, I am told, a matter of taste.

choices.label: Sell all three to the Temple.
choices.reply: Splendid. Rivals are expensive. Temple justice is ruinous. I shall send flowers.

choices.label: Burn all three. The river has had enough.
choices.reply: A merciful fool, or a very clever one. I shall decide over breakfast.

quests.outro: The Odai ran as it always had, and nobody on either bank could say who owned it.

quests.title: The Temple Reads the River
quests.desc: The ledgers are in the Temple. Witnesses are needed, and the factor's rival is not happy.

objectives.text: Ask the bridge guard to escort the witnesses
objectives.topic: The Temple wants witnesses crossing the bridge by morning.
objectives.reply: Then they will be crossing under my eye. I am not hiring a protector, sera; I am being thorough. Come at dawn and walk where I say.

objectives.text: Break the rival's attempt to drown the witnesses

quests.outro: The witnesses reached the Temple dry and rather annoyed.

quests.title: Ash on the Odai
quests.desc: The ledgers burned. The people they ruined want to say thank you, and some others want to ask why.

objectives.text: Meet Nilena at the south-bank steps
objectives.topic: It is done. The ledgers are ash.
objectives.reply: Then somebody I know is out of debt, and somebody I used to know is out of work. I have a mind to throw a dinner. Go and make sure nobody throws a knife.

objectives.text: Defend the south-bank steps from the ruined bookkeeper's men

quests.outro: Balmora ate well that night, and nobody asked for a receipt.

quests.title: The Strider Who Wouldn't Walk
quests.offer: Do you have a calm voice? A very, very calm voice?
quests.pitch: Old Dowager has not moved in six days. A strider will not stand still for six days unless it is sulking, ill, or sitting on something. I have checked sulking. Take a lantern and a bucket of sorrow and have a look under her.
quests.desc: Port-Master Orrel has a silt strider that will not budge, and he suspects something beneath her.

objectives.text: Examine the strider in the caravan yard
objectives.journal: A neat square hole under her middle leg, packed with silk. Somebody dug here and has been coming back at night.

objectives.text: Catch the smugglers coming back for their cache
Tell Orrel what Dowager was guarding
objectives.topic: She was sitting on a smuggler's cache. Silk and skooma.
objectives.reply: Then she is a better citizen than half this town. Keep the silk, report the skooma, and for pity's sake, do not tell her she has been brave. It goes to her head.

quests.outro: Dowager rose the next morning with a long, sceptical sigh.

quests.title: The Ninth Plate
quests.offer: You are hungry. Sit. No, not that seat. That one has a reservation.
quests.pitch: Eight plates a night, no more. The ninth person goes hungry. Tonight she is a girl in a grey cloak who will not take charity, only work. She needs a letter carried to a boat at the west docks and she says it will end badly for whoever carries it. I would like it to end better.
quests.desc: Sirela Marvos of Eight Plates wants a nameless girl's letter delivered to a ship, safely.

objectives.text: Take the letter from the ninth guest
objectives.topic: I will carry it for her.
objectives.reply: It is addressed to nobody and sealed in plain wax. Mind the Hlaalu men at the bridge; they have been asking after a grey cloak.

objectives.text: Get through the bridge-watch asking after a grey cloak
Give the letter to the silt-strider captain
objectives.topic: This is for the west-dock boat.
objectives.reply: A letter for nobody. I have been waiting two years for this letter. The boat leaves tonight, and she will be on it. You never saw her.

quests.outro: The ninth plate was set out the next night too, and nobody sat at it.

quests.title: The Honour of the Shell
quests.offer: You have the look of a witness. Are you one?
quests.pitch: A duel will be fought at the gate of the Skar at the second bell. Two Redoran cousins, one old grievance. I need a witness who owes neither house a favour, because I suspect the grievance is not what the cousins believe it is. Watch the blades. Particularly the blades.
quests.desc: Councilor Brara needs an impartial witness to a Redoran duel at the gate of the Skar.

objectives.text: Witness the duel at the gate of the Skar
objectives.journal: The cousins bowed, crossed blades, and one of them stumbled backward, clutching a scratch no deeper than a thorn-prick. He was dead before the second bell had rung.

objectives.text: Ask the guard-captain to examine the blade
objectives.topic: A scratch should not kill a man. May I see the blade?
objectives.reply: A scratch will not. Resin on a blade might. It is a poison, not a weapon of honour, and honour is the one thing the Redoran may not forgive. Take it to the apothecary, Tevra Dren, quietly.

objectives.text: Show Tevra the blade
objectives.topic: What is this resin? Whose receipt?
objectives.reply: Kwama-egg resin, boiled and thickened. Only one kind of person has a vat like that: a miner with a grudge and a licence. Try the egg-mine tunnels, below the Skar, behind the third gallery.

objectives.text: Track the poisoner into the egg-mine tunnels
Corner Rilu the Shell-Poisoner
Take the poisoner's jar and the receipt
Present the proof to the Council
objectives.topic: Councilor, here is the poisoner, the vat, and the buyer.
objectives.reply: My own cousin bought it. Twice. And paid with a House ring. Under Redoran law the accused may demand a duel; I may accept in his place, or I may stand down and let him defend his own name. Which shall it be, witness?

choices.label: Accept the duel in his place. Let the Council see you fight.
choices.reply: It will be a good evening. Bring a cloak; the shell is cold.

choices.label: Make him answer for himself. Let the Council judge.
choices.reply: Then he stands before his peers with nothing but his name. It is the harsher sentence, and the more honest.

quests.outro: Redoran honour was satisfied, and the shell stood as it has stood for ages.

quests.title: A Duel Before the Council
quests.desc: Councilor Brara has accepted a formal duel in the cousin's place, and you are her second.

objectives.text: Seek Durgul Ash-Born for the formal rules
objectives.topic: I am to second a duel before the Council. Teach me the rite.
objectives.reply: Three rules. Do not strike a man who has yielded. Do not yield to a man who has not struck. Do not look at the Council, because they will be looking at you, and it is vulgar to look back.

objectives.text: Second Councilor Brara in the formal duel

quests.outro: The champion yielded; the Council was silent a long time, then they struck the floor with their staves, which in Ald'ruhn is applause.

quests.title: The Rat in the Pot, Honestly
quests.offer: You look like you have eaten somewhere worse than here.
quests.pitch: There was a rat. It's on the sign. Last week a Council inspector found the sign, found the rat, and fined me for 'advertising a pest.' Prove the rat is a mascot, not a menace. The fine is nine drakes a day and my tolerance for this is limited.
quests.desc: Nerva Hlavis of the Rat in the Pot is being fined for her sign. She wants proof the rat is a mascot, not a pest.

objectives.text: Ask Brarmin who first called the pot rat-infested
objectives.topic: Who reported the Rat in the Pot?
objectives.reply: Reported? The inspector's cousin runs the tavern across the way: the Skar's Last Word. Only a very jealous man could notice a sign that high up. Bring a witness who has eaten here for years. That would be me, sera, and I am free at the second bell.

objectives.text: Bring the Council inspector to the pot for an honest tasting
objectives.journal: The inspector came, ate three bowls, and could not stop staring at the sign. He did not leave a tip. He left an apology.

objectives.text: Report the result to Nerva
objectives.topic: The inspector has withdrawn the fine.
objectives.reply: Then we have both survived an honest day. I will name a stew for you. Do not ask which one; it is the one nobody orders.

quests.outro: The sign still has a rat on it. It now has a very small crown.

quests.title: Whistle Not Under the Shell
quests.offer: You do not whistle, do you? Say you do not whistle.
quests.pitch: The shell has ribs, sera, and the ribs have hollows, and the hollows hum when the wind is right. Last night a new note came up through the floor of my cellar. Not a hum. A tune. Three notes, and the third was wrong. I do not like a song I have not been taught.
quests.desc: Brarmin the egg-miner hears a tune rising from the tunnels beneath the Skar.

objectives.text: Follow the three-note tune down into the old egg tunnels
objectives.journal: The wrong third note comes from a row of clay pipes set into the wall, tuned to the wind. Somebody has built a flute that plays the whole shell.

objectives.text: Silence what has gathered to listen
Tell Brarmin what you found
objectives.topic: Pipes in the wall. A tune only the wind could play.
objectives.reply: Then it was a prank by dead masons, and it will ring on the ninth day of every Sun's Dusk. I shall hang a bell in the cellar. If it chimes the third note, I will whistle the right one.

quests.outro: The shell sings on certain nights, and everyone in Ald'ruhn now knows the proper third note.

quests.title: A Bet Between Towers
quests.offer: You have a face that has never won anything. Wonderful.
quests.pitch: I have wagered Magister Ulveni that a stranger can lift her singing teapot from her fourteenth floor in a single night. She says no. She says it with a number of guardians. Take the slip, cross the rope-bridges, and bring me the pot. If you lose, you will lose in an interesting way. I shall enjoy it.
quests.desc: Magister Gaenor Dreth has bet his neighbour Ulveni that someone can steal her singing teapot. He chose you.

objectives.text: Accept the wager
objectives.topic: Where is the tower and what is the catch?
objectives.reply: Tel Naga. Four rope-bridges, one levitation gap that you cannot cross without a little something, and a guardian she will not name. The something is this potion. It will carry you six paces. Plan your landing.

objectives.text: Cross four rope bridges to Ulveni's tower
objectives.journal: The ropes sang under my boots. On the fourth I looked down, which was a mistake; the lagoon is a long way off and the fungi are cheerfully luminous.

objectives.text: Cross the levitation gap and answer the lesser guardians
Defeat the tower's resident spell-guard
Take the singing teapot from the fourteenth floor
Face Magister Ulveni with her teapot
objectives.topic: Magister. Your teapot. I would like to know what you say next.
objectives.reply: I say: how delightful, and: do put it down, it is sulking. My rival wagered I could not be robbed. Now I have a choice, and I find I would like to make you make it. Return it to me and I owe you a favour. Take it to him, and he owes me one. Ha. Ha. Which favour would you prefer to be at the centre of?

choices.label: Return it to Ulveni. Let Gaenor lose his wager.
choices.reply: Gaenor, you old tide-pool. Look who won. You owe me a tower's worth of embarrassment.

choices.label: Bring it to Gaenor. The bet is the bet.
choices.reply: Honourable and tedious. He will be unbearable for a month. Go; I shall hold a grudge on your behalf.

quests.outro: The teapot hummed three notes at dusk. Both Magisters claimed it was in tune.

quests.title: A Magister's Favour
quests.desc: Magister Ulveni owes you a favour and wants it spent quickly, on something small and impertinent.

objectives.text: Collect your favour
objectives.topic: You said you owed me one.
objectives.reply: I did. I would like to cash it in your name. Go to Gaenor's tower and swap his chair for a wash-basin. Quickly. He believes in sitting a certain way.

objectives.text: Swap Gaenor's chair in the Council Spire terrace

quests.outro: Gaenor sat with great dignity in a wash-basin for nearly a minute before noticing.

quests.title: Gaenor's Prize
quests.desc: Magister Gaenor won the wager and feels the need to celebrate, loudly, in a place with an audience.

objectives.text: Join the Magister's celebration
objectives.topic: You won. Now what?
objectives.reply: Now I take the pot to the Gateway Inn and play it for the room. Mind the crowd; some of them are Ulveni's, and her people are poor losers. Stand with me at the bar.

objectives.text: Break Ulveni's sulking partisans at the Gateway Inn

quests.outro: The teapot played, the crowd sang, and the inn needed new windows by morning.

quests.title: The Apprentice Who Wanted Out
quests.offer: Can you read a contract? A really nasty one?
quests.pitch: My indenture says I serve Magister Ulveni for ten years, and in the fine print, three more if she has a 'significant disappointment'. I have been a disappointment since the first spring. Find the clause that lets me go, or the person who wrote it, and I will carry your bags for the rest of my life. Which is, I hope, short.
quests.desc: Apprentice Veya wants out of her ten-year indenture to Magister Ulveni.

objectives.text: Ask the garrison clerk for the registry copy
objectives.topic: Veya's apprenticeship contract is registered with the Legion. Can I see it?
objectives.reply: Registered by a Telvanni notary and countersigned by a Legion clerk who is no longer in the Legion. I recall him. He had a wooden hand and a tendency to forget himself near rope-bridges. His practice was a few steps west of Sadrith, in the old customs shed.

objectives.text: Find the notary's shed at the lagoon's edge
objectives.journal: A shed full of ink and dust. The notary kept a second copy of every contract and filed every clause under its loophole. I found Veya's. The loophole reads: "Void upon the Magister's first apology."

objectives.text: Ask Ulveni to apologise
objectives.topic: Veya's indenture ends the day you apologise. To anyone.
objectives.reply: Ha. Hahaha. A clause. Good lord. I have not apologised since the Second Era. Leave me. I shall think it over. Come back when I have found a way to apologise to a fish.

choices.label: Wait. She will find a way.
choices.reply: A fish, a fungus and a rope-bridge got the best of me. Veya. You are free. I am a monster.

choices.label: Don't give her the satisfaction. Tell her to apologise to the lagoon.
choices.reply: The lagoon accepts. Hmph. Veya, you are, regrettably, free.

objectives.text: Tell Veya she is free
objectives.topic: It is done. You are no one's apprentice.
objectives.reply: Then I am no one. Is that what it feels like? It feels like holding my breath and finding I do not need to. Thank you. I shall go to Mournhold. I shall learn to read other people's handwriting.

quests.outro: Veya left Sadrith before the fish heard.

quests.title: The Grey Strain
quests.offer: Do you have a strong stomach? Asking for a mushroom.
quests.pitch: I grew a grey cap in the back greenhouse that does not belong to anything. It does not glow, it does not sing, and the room around it is very quiet in a way I do not like. It is eating the other spores. Help me contain it. Do not touch it. Do not look at the gills.
quests.desc: Skeema the Sporekeeper grew a new grey strain that eats the glowing gardens.

objectives.text: Clear the fumigation chambers of what the strain has woken
Ask Fennik Sul for fumigation salts
objectives.topic: Skeema needs strong salts. Anything that kills a spore.
objectives.reply: I have the salts, I have the jars, and I have my doubts. I will sell you three measures at cost, which is a joke, because I have never once sold anything at cost. Do not tell anyone.

objectives.text: Decide the strain's fate with Skeema
objectives.topic: The grey cap is isolated. Burn it, or keep a cutting?
objectives.reply: I want to burn it. Every sensible part of me wants to burn it. But it is the first thing in my life that has surprised me in thirty years. Choose for me, because I shall regret it either way.

choices.label: Burn it. All of it.
choices.reply: The garden breathes again. I shall plant the blue ones where it grew and call it a lesson.

choices.label: Keep one cutting, sealed, for study.
choices.reply: In the cellar. Under three locks. Under four. I shall call it the Quiet One and never speak of it.

quests.outro: The back greenhouse is very quiet now, and Skeema checks it twice before every dawn.

quests.title: The Window That Lied
quests.offer: Do you believe in rooms that do not stay put?
quests.pitch: Number nine's window showed the lagoon on Monday and the Ascadian Isles on Tuesday and, last night, a woman in a green shawl, waving. She waved at a guest who never checked in. The Magisters say it is a 'resonance.' I say it is a ghost with a view. Find who she is.
quests.desc: Dalyne Hlaren of the Gateway Inn has a window that shows a woman who is not there.

objectives.text: Sit in room nine and watch the window at dusk
objectives.journal: At dusk the lagoon dissolved and a woman in a green shawl stood in a field of white flowers. She did not wave. She pointed, west and a little down.

objectives.text: Follow where she pointed, to the base of the tower
objectives.journal: A single stone, half-buried, with a shawl-pin at its foot. The engraving reads: "Waited here. Was never met."

objectives.text: Bring the pin to Dalyne
objectives.topic: She was waiting for someone who never arrived. Here is her pin.
objectives.reply: Then I shall set a second place at room nine each Sundas, and a fresh flower in the window. The Magisters can explain the resonance as they wish; I have a ghost with a reservation.

quests.outro: Room nine now has a green shawl on the chair, and nobody is ever charged for it.

quests.title: A Grave Not Dug
quests.offer: The gravedigger will not speak to me. Perhaps he will speak to you.
quests.pitch: Aldrin has dug four hundred graves in this town and tonight he laid down his spade and said he would not dig one more. Someone has asked him for a grave and he will not say whose. Ask him. He is a stubborn man, but he is also a sad one, and sad men tell strangers what they cannot tell the Keeper.
quests.desc: Keeper Salvu says the gravedigger Aldrin has refused to dig one grave and will not say whose.

objectives.text: Ask Aldrin whose grave he will not dig
objectives.topic: Salvu says you put down your spade. For whom?
objectives.reply: A Sathil. Dead forty years and no one buried her. Her bones lie in the family tomb with the door sealed from inside. I will not dig the grave she was meant to have, because I would be digging in her place. Her son is the heir and he has not been home since the fire.

objectives.text: Track the Sathil heir to the plantation's farm
objectives.journal: A farmstead gone to bracken. A man sleeps in the barn with a half-burned deed in his fist, and a ring on his thumb he does not remove even to wash.

objectives.text: Ask Elder Nerevi about the heir
objectives.topic: The heir is a Sathil. Why will no one let him home?
objectives.reply: Because he left, sera, in the fire year, when his mother was still breathing. A son who runs while his mother lies in the house is a ghost that has not yet died. We do not speak to him. We do not speak of him. Take this to the tomb, if you must go.

objectives.text: Retrieve the Sathil ash from the sealed tomb
Face the unburied Sathil
Bring the ash to Keeper Salvu
objectives.topic: The ash is warm. The heir sleeps in a barn. What now?
objectives.reply: Now we may bury her, or we may let the line lapse; that is not mine to decide, and I would not decide it for the son. But you have walked among the dead on his behalf. You may speak for him. Choose, for him.

choices.label: Bury her. Let the son stand at the grave.
choices.reply: Then the Row has thirteen houses again. I shall tell Aldrin to find his spade.

choices.label: Let the line lapse. Scatter the ash on the farm.
choices.reply: It is old law, and a gentle one. The farm will bear well. She will see to it.

quests.outro: The next morning, Aldrin was seen walking toward the Row, carrying a spade and humming.

quests.title: The Widow Who Guards the Row
quests.offer: You walked among the Sathil dead. Then perhaps you are not an outlander.
quests.pitch: My husband lies in the third house. Every night a stranger leaves a candle at his door, an outlander's candle, plain wax, without a name. I cannot tell whether it is an insult or a prayer. Learn who it is. If it is a prayer, I will let you walk the Row. If it is an insult, I will have a word with the Keeper.
quests.desc: Elder Nerevi wants to know who leaves plain candles at her husband's tomb.

objectives.text: Wait at the third house of the Row at midnight
objectives.journal: A hooded figure arrived with a plain wax candle and lit it with shaking hands. She did not see me. She said one word: "Sorry."

objectives.text: Ask Tadrik who buys plain wax candles
objectives.topic: Someone buys a plain candle every night. Who?
objectives.reply: A young woman, a Legion cook's daughter, I believe. Her father was a Legion man who died on the same night as Nerevi's husband, in the same fire. She thinks she owes the old woman an apology for something she cannot name.

objectives.text: Tell Elder Nerevi
objectives.topic: The candle is a prayer. A Legion cook's daughter, grieving.
objectives.reply: Then I have been angry at a mourner. That is a thing a widow does not like to learn. Tell her to come in daylight. Tell her the Row is open.

choices.label: I will.
choices.reply: Thank you. And you, sera. You may walk the Row. Mind the third step; my husband did.

quests.outro: In daylight, a young woman and an old one stood at the third house and said nothing for a long time.

quests.title: The Candle Count
quests.offer: Count with me. Do you count in threes? Good.
quests.pitch: Every night I put out forty-one candles in the alcoves. Every morning I find forty-two. I do not mind the extra, but one more tomorrow might be a guest and not a candle, and I do not know how to charge a guest who is not in the book.
quests.desc: Mirele Sathil of the Pilgrims' Rest finds one more candle each morning than she put out.

objectives.text: Keep watch in the hostel alcoves overnight
objectives.journal: Between the fourth and fifth bell, a candle lit itself in the alcove at the end. The shape beside it was a child, sitting with her knees up, looking at the flame.

objectives.text: Ask Keeper Salvu about the child
objectives.topic: A girl in the far alcove. She lights a candle and watches it.
objectives.reply: A pilgrim's daughter, nine years dead, who never reached the shrine. Her family walked on and never knew. Her candle is her request. Put a chair by it and say her name aloud. She wants to hear it said by someone who is not family.

objectives.text: Tell Mirele what the child wants
objectives.topic: Her name is Dahlia. She wants a chair and her name said aloud.
objectives.reply: Then I shall say it every night at the forty-second candle. Dahlia. There. That is not hard. I should have asked.

quests.outro: The forty-second candle now has a small chair beside it, and a card with a single name.

quests.title: The Channel Runs Hot
quests.offer: Do you mind heat? Good. Do you mind losses?
quests.pitch: A heat-vent failed last night in the Underworks. The channel ran twenty degrees over and a lava-flow touched a cold room. Nobody died. Yet. Look at the vent, take the lift down, and put out whatever has woken in the pool. Do not touch the glass.
quests.desc: Warden Ilu Dren of the canton lift wants a failed heat-vent examined and a magma creature put out.

objectives.text: Examine the failed heat-vent beside the temple stair
objectives.journal: The baffle was cracked in one straight line. Someone cut it. Nothing hot makes a crack that clean.

objectives.text: Ask Dren the Lavacutter about the cut
objectives.topic: The baffle was cut, not cracked. By whom?
objectives.reply: Not whom. What. A salt-cutter, bone-handled, the kind the glassworkers use. A man who wants a channel hotter wants one of three things: a cold room melted, a quiet grave, or a reason to sell insurance.

objectives.text: Descend to the Underworks through the lift and clear the vents
Lure the Slag-Heart into the quenching pool
Return to Warden Ilu with the core
objectives.topic: The vent is sealed. But to seal it I must close the lift's lower station. That leaves forty families without a quick way down.
objectives.reply: A quiet station. A longer stair. I knew it would cost something. Do I close it, and lose forty families their trade, or leave it open and risk the next flood? I would like someone else to say the word.

choices.label: Close the lower station. Safety first.
choices.reply: Then forty families climb a hundred extra stairs for the rest of their lives, and none will die in the heat. I will write it in the book.

choices.label: Keep it open, and put a guard on the vent every night.
choices.reply: A guard is cheaper than a stair. It means I am the guard. I accept it; I wanted a reason to stop sleeping.

quests.outro: The Underworks glowed a little dimmer that night, and a little safer.

quests.title: What the Living Leave Behind
quests.offer: Have you left anything behind lately? A footprint, a sigh?
quests.pitch: Someone has stolen my ash-lantern, the one with everyone's little bit in it. A thief of ashes is a thief of everyone's good name. It was last seen on the harbour tunnels' ledge. Bring it back, and do not open the shutter. It is not for you.
quests.desc: Sister Mavia's ash-lantern has been stolen from the canton. She wants it back, unopened.

objectives.text: Search the harbour tunnels for the lantern-thief
Take the ash-lantern from the thief's cache
Return the lantern to Mavia
objectives.topic: The shutter is closed. It was not opened.
objectives.reply: Thank you. You know, nobody has ever asked me what I do with the ash. I plant it. Along the cliff road, one thimble at a time. The lilies there are the oddest shade. That is all of you, and all of us, and I thought it would be kind to say.

quests.outro: A new row of pale lilies appears along the cliff road each spring.

quests.title: Paying for the Cooling
quests.offer: You look hot. That will be four drakes.
quests.pitch: A charge for cooling is a joke, sera, a joke my father made and I inherited, but now a Redoran inspector wants it banned and a Hlaalu competitor wants it franchised. I would like both to see sense, or at least each other. Bring them to the same table.
quests.desc: Orvyn Hlaalo of the Cinder Cup wants a Redoran inspector and a Hlaalu competitor brought to one table.

objectives.text: Carry an invitation to the Hlaalu competitor
objectives.topic: Orvyn invites you for soup. Bring your lawyers, he says.
objectives.reply: Soup. I have not had soup in this town in years. Tell him I will come, and tell him I will bring a notary, a bodyguard and my appetite, in that order of importance.

objectives.text: Carry an invitation to the Redoran inspector
objectives.topic: Orvyn invites you for soup, Warden.
objectives.reply: A Redoran at table with a Hlaalu is a curiosity. I shall attend, as a neutral. Neutral parties eat slowly.

objectives.text: Report back to Orvyn
objectives.topic: They are both coming.
objectives.reply: Then I shall serve the soup with ladle and flourish and charge them four drakes each for the cooling. Do not tell them it is a joke. A joke is only funny if no one is warned.

quests.outro: Both parties left friends, or at least bored with each other, which in Molag Mar counts.

quests.title: The Bastion and the Quarter
quests.offer: You are not Legion, not Dunmer, not Company. Good. You are nobody.
quests.pitch: Someone is selling keys to the Dunmer quarter gate. A key buys a night's entry, a barrel's smuggling, a knife in the dark. I want the seller's name by sunrise and I would like it delivered quietly. A man who is arrested by rumour is a martyr by morning. Go in, ask, come out. Do not wear Legion colours.
quests.desc: Legate Corvus Pello wants the name of whoever is selling gate keys into the Dunmer quarter.

objectives.text: Ask Aryn the Informer who sells the keys
objectives.topic: Someone sells gate keys. Who?
objectives.reply: Not 'who', sera, 'which'. There are three sellers and one customer. The customer is a Legion officer who buys one on the first of every month. I do not name officers for free.

objectives.text: Slip into the Dunmer quarter and watch the south gate
objectives.journal: At the third bell a guard unlocked the south gate, took a purse from a shadow and said nothing. He did not look back. He locked it again after the shadow had passed.

objectives.text: Turn the guard who sells the keys
objectives.topic: I saw you sell the south gate. I am not Legion. Tell me why.
objectives.reply: My mother is sick. The Legion pays in coin that does not arrive. I sell the gate; I do not sell the walls. Please. Take this list, and this key. And tell no one my mother's name.

objectives.text: Bring the list to Legate Corvus
objectives.topic: Here is your name. And your buyer.
objectives.reply: A guard, sixty drakes, a sick mother. I could have him flogged in the square. I could burn the list and let the gate go on as it has. Or I could keep the list, and have you walk it to the Quarter Elders instead. I will take the lesson you give me.

choices.label: Arrest the guard and publish the list.
choices.reply: Order restored. The Quarter will remember me as the man who punished a son for his mother. I will bear it.

choices.label: Disarm the plot. Take the list to the Quarter Elders instead.
choices.reply: The Elders will decide, and decide wisely, which I could not. You have wasted the Legion's time and saved it from a mistake.

quests.outro: The south gate was locked properly that week, and a sick woman was found a physician.

quests.title: The Customs Yard Parrot
quests.offer: Do you speak parrot? No? A shame. Neither does anyone here.
quests.pitch: A Company parrot has been repeating a sum in the customs yard for three days. Nobody knows what it means. It is either a ransom, a price, or a lottery. It is four hundred and twelve drakes, repeated every ten minutes, in a Hlaalu accent. Find out whose.
quests.desc: Felmin Rothal wants to know what the Company parrot's repeated sum means.

objectives.text: Listen to the parrot in the customs yard
objectives.journal: The parrot says: "Four hundred and twelve. Silk. Pay at dusk. Do not tell the Factor." Then it says a name I cannot print.

objectives.text: Ask Aryn whose voice the parrot copies
objectives.topic: The parrot speaks like a Hlaalu clerk. Which?
objectives.reply: A clerk named Vedran, fired last month for double-booking. He has been paying the dockhands to forward the silk his way. The parrot was his; he left it behind. Parrots, sera, are very poor at keeping secrets.

objectives.text: Tell Felmin
objectives.topic: The sum is a smuggled silk shipment. Vedran, the sacked clerk.
objectives.reply: A dishonest clerk undone by a bird. I shall give the bird a promotion. A small one. A cracker and a perch.

quests.outro: The parrot now says "Order. Order. Order." in a very flat voice.

quests.title: A Quiet War of Confessions
quests.offer: Do you confess? I do not ask, but I hear.
quests.pitch: Three of the garrison have confessed the same sin this week, in three different words: a night off the walls, a gate left open, and a lamp left lit. Each was told to speak to no one. I must break the seal if I am to prevent it. I need an outsider to ask where they were, without ever asking.
quests.desc: Chaplain Loris needs an outsider to learn why three guards confessed the same sin.

objectives.text: Watch the garrison walls at the lamp-lighting hour
objectives.journal: At dusk the three guards left their posts together, crossed the bridge without speaking, and stood in a field of ash-flowers looking at a small stone. They did not pray. They saluted.

objectives.text: Ask Marga Ironhand about the stone
objectives.topic: Three guards salute a stone in the ash-flowers. Whose?
objectives.reply: Their fourth. Died last winter on a night watch when the lamp went out. They each left their post to tend a lamp for him. They would be flogged for it. They would do it again. Do not tell the Legate.

objectives.text: Tell Chaplain Loris
objectives.topic: It is a lamp for a dead comrade. Nothing worse.
objectives.reply: Then I shall confess it for them, in the only way I can: I shall relight the lamp myself at the right hour, and let the walls think it is routine. Bless you. And bless a very quiet war.

quests.outro: The garrison lamp has not gone out since.
